title: Sport and Simulation handling for ATVs and motorcycles
summary: In a local ride, open Settings → Game Settings → Physics. Sport gives the tires more grip for fast corners. Simulation makes it easier to use up the grip available for turning when accelerating or braking.
details: Wheelspin carries through a jump and meets the ground through the tire contact. The ATV applies forces at all four wheels. The motorcycle banks toward the combined support force as it corners. Sport eases the throttle during excessive wheelspin.

The motorcycle rider shifts at the hips, braces under braking and absorbs the bike rising over bumps. Hands track the bars and a sliding boot eases off its peg. The same weight shift affects balance. The ATV rider braces into corners, and rear-tire scrub changes how much dirt the bike throws.

Hard, deep landings gradually weaken individual dampers. Sustained tire scrub consumes tread. Repeated braking heats the brakes and can cause fade. The rotors glow as brakes heat up and dim as they cool. A fresh ride or race restart supplies fresh components.
limitation: These are game-tuned models. Verification uses synthetic force and braking tests and private-content host rides. Instrumented vehicle calibration, rider playtesting and physical-phone measurements remain open. Online rooms use Original.
caption: Brake heat appears as red-orange rotor rings on the ATV’s visible wheels after a stop.
